t.6.54.1: He roared a mighty roar, making the ocean resound, as though producing thunderclaps and as though shattering the mountains.
t.6.54.3: But seeing them fleeing, Aṅgada, the son of Vālin, spoke to Nala, Nīla, Gavākṣa and the mighty Kumuda.
t.6.54.2: Seeing him approach, fearsome-eyed and impossible to slay even for Maghavan, Yama and Varuṇa, the vānaras fled in all directions.
t.6.54.4: Forgetting yourselves here, your valour and your noble lineage, where are you going, stricken with fear, like common monkeys?
t.6.54.5: Come, good friends, turn back! Why do you try so hard to save your lives? This rākṣasa is surely no match for battle; he is only a great bogey meant to frighten.
t.6.54.6: This great terror of the Rākṣasas that has arisen, we shall blow away by our valor; turn back, O monkeys!
t.6.54.7: But having with difficulty reassured one another and gathered together from here and there, the monkeys, with trees and rocks in their hands, set out for the field of battle.
t.6.54.8: Turning back, those mighty forest-dwellers, enraged and utterly furious like elephants in rut, struck Kumbhakarṇa with lofty mountain peaks and with rocks.
t.6.54.9: Though struck with trees whose tops were in blossom, he did not tremble; the rocks that fell upon his limbs were shattered into hundreds of pieces, and the trees with flowering tops fell broken upon the surface of the earth.
t.6.54.10: He too, greatly enraged and exerting himself to the utmost, churned up the armies of the mighty vānaras, like a fire that has flared up among the forests.
t.6.54.11: Many bulls among the monkeys lie wet with blood, struck down and fallen upon the ground, like trees bearing copper-red flowers.
t.6.54.12: Leaping and running headlong, the monkeys did not look back; some fell into the ocean, while others took to the sky.
t.6.54.13: But those heroes, being struck down by the mightier rākṣasa, fled back by that very path by which they had crossed the ocean.
t.6.54.14: With faces downcast from fear, they fled to the high ground and likewise to the low; the bears climbed up into the trees, and some took refuge on the mountain.
t.6.54.15: Some of the monkeys plunged into the ocean, some took refuge in caves; some sank down where they were, and some could not stand their ground at all.
t.6.54.16: Seeing those monkeys broken and fleeing, Aṅgada spoke these words: "Stand firm, let us fight! Turn back, O monkeys!"
t.6.54.17: Even if I were to traverse this whole earth, I see no place of refuge for you once you are routed. Turn back, all of you! Why do you try to save your lives?
t.6.54.18: O you whose movement and valour are unhindered, your wives will surely laugh at you as you flee without your weapons; that indeed is a mortal blow, so let one go on living thus!
t.6.54.19: All of you were born in great and widespread families; truly it is ignoble that, frightened, you cast aside your valor and run away!
t.6.54.20: Those boasts of yours that you once made in the assembly of the people, so lofty and so great, where have they now gone?
t.6.54.21: Words of reproach are heard against the coward, and he who lives on is despised. Let the path trodden by good men be followed; let fear be cast aside.
t.6.54.22: Either we shall lie slain upon the earth, our lives cut short, or, struck down in battle, we shall attain the world of Brahmā so hard to reach; or else, having slain the enemy in combat, we may win glory.
t.6.54.23: Kumbhakarṇa, having seen Kākutstha, will not go away alive, just as a moth that has reached a blazing fire does not.
t.6.54.25: Then the fleeing monkeys spoke to the heroic Aṅgada, adorned with golden armlets, as he was speaking thus, words that the brave would condemn.
t.6.54.24: Marked out by our flight, we are saving our lives; many have been routed by one alone, and our fame will go to ruin.
t.6.54.26: A terrible slaughter has been wrought upon us by the rākṣasa Kumbhakarṇa. This is no time to stand fast; we are going, for our lives are dear to us.
t.6.54.27: Having spoken only these words, all those leaders of the monkey troops, seeing the terrible one with fearsome eyes approaching, fled in every direction.
t.6.54.28: Then all those heroic monkeys who were fleeing were turned back by Aṅgada with words of comfort and with many marks of honour.
t.6.54.29: Ṛṣabha, Śarabha, Mainda, Dhūmra and Nīla, Kumuda, Suṣeṇa, Gavākṣa, Rambha and Tāra, with Dvivida, Panasa and the son of Vāyu foremost among them, set out with the utmost speed straight toward the battle.
